text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- World trade ministers close to deal on labour standards.
- The European Union urged by an advisory group to focus more trade and investments in Asian markets.
- A Singapore $13 million estate of businessman who died more than 70 years ago being claimed by possibly more than 300 descendants.
- Asian markets fall in line with Wall Streets's drop.
- Hong Kong tycoon Richard Li's Pacific Century Regional Development buys Singapore bungalow site for S$112 million.
- US producer prices show little signs of inflation.
- Major breakthrough expected in WTO declaration, consensus reached on controversial issues.
- Information Technology Agreement in the bag at WTO conference with at least 29 nations to sign intention to eliminate tariffs on most IT products by year 2000.
- Singapore exporters, who make up for one-tenth of world's IT products, to gain market access and save millions in tariff payments after global pact sealed at WTO.
- Pacific Century, controlled by Hong Kong tycoon Richard Li, buys Singapore bungalow site for S$112 million.
- Hong Kong-listed Sum Cheong International expects to resume trading soon after shares suspended since February 1.
- Consortium led by unit of Singapore Airlines has US$140 million deal to lease a Boeing 747-400 freighter aircraft to Asiana Airlines of South Korea.
